checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is the quotient polynomial Q(X) = f(X)/Z(X) correctly computed in compute_kzg_proof_multi_impl before committing to KZG_SETUP_G1_MONOMIAL?

reachability.notes: KZG proof generation is triggered for every blob submitted. The proof must be correctly computed for the data availability guarantee to hold.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify all client implementations of compute_kzg_proof_multi_impl (c-kzg-4844, go-kzg-4844, rust-kzg, etc.). 2. Verify that the quotient polynomial is computed as divide_polynomialcoeff(polynomial_coeff, denominator_poly) where denominator_poly = vanishing_polynomialcoeff(zs). 3. Confirm that the simplification Q(X) = f(X)/Z(X) (instead of Q(X) = (f(X) - I(X))/Z(X)) is only applied when deg(I(X)) < deg(Z(X)), which holds because I(X) is degree k-1 and Z(X) is degree k. 4. Construct a test blob where the polynomial has specific known coefficients and manually compute Q(X) to verify the implementation matches. 5. Test with edge cases: zero polynomial, polynomial with all-zero evaluations at the coset, polynomial whose degree equals FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB. 6. Verify that the g1_lincomb uses exactly len(quotient_polynomial) elements from KZG_SETUP_G1_MONOMIAL and not more or fewer. 7. Confirm the resulting KZG proof passes verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch for correctly computed cells.

Computes Z(X) = product of (X - x_i) for all evaluation points. Incorrect vanishing polynomial would invalidate all proofs.

Any error in polynomial division or vanishing polynomial construction produces invalid proofs, breaking data availability guarantees.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is the vanishing polynomial Z(X) correctly constructed over the cell coset evaluation points?

reachability.notes: The vanishing polynomial defines the evaluation domain. If incorrect, Q(X) is wrong and proofs are invalid.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. For each cell index i in [0, CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB), compute the coset via coset_for_cell(i) and verify it returns the correct FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_CELL (64) evaluation points. 2. Verify vanishing_polynomialcoeff correctly computes the product polynomial P(X) = product(X - x_i) by checking that evaluating the result at each x_i yields zero. 3. Confirm that the vanishing polynomial has degree exactly equal to FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_CELL (64). 4. Test for potential overflow or modular arithmetic errors in multiply_polynomialcoeff when building the vanishing polynomial iteratively. 5. Verify that coset_shift_for_cell returns the correct coset generator h such that coset = {h * omega^i} for roots of unity omega. 6. Confirm that PRIMITIVE_ROOT_OF_UNITY is correctly used as the coset shift factor. 7. Check that no two cells share overlapping coset points (cosets must be disjoint for the erasure coding to work).

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is the KZG proof commitment g1_lincomb(KZG_SETUP_G1_MONOMIAL[:len(Q)], Q) correctly computed using the trusted setup?

reachability.notes: The final proof is a commitment to Q(X) using the trusted setup. Incorrect linear combination or wrong SRS slice invalidates the proof.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Verify that g1_lincomb correctly computes the multi-scalar multiplication (MSM) of quotient polynomial coefficients with KZG_SETUP_G1_MONOMIAL elements. 2. Confirm that exactly len(quotient_polynomial) elements are taken from KZG_SETUP_G1_MONOMIAL (not more, not fewer). 3. Test edge case where quotient polynomial has trailing zero coefficients -- verify these do not cause incorrect SRS slice selection. 4. Verify the KZG_SETUP_G1_MONOMIAL is loaded correctly from the trusted setup file and has sufficient length (at least FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB elements). 5. Test with known test vectors: for a simple polynomial f(X) = X, compute the expected proof manually and compare. 6. Check for off-by-one errors in the SRS slicing: KZG_SETUP_G1_MONOMIAL[:len(Q)] should include indices 0 through len(Q)-1. 7. Verify that the g1_lincomb implementation handles the point-at-infinity correctly (ref: c-kzg-4844 issue #603). 8. Check that precompute optimizations (FK20) produce identical proofs to the naive O(n^2) implementation.

Verify that fft_field with inv=True correctly computes the inverse by multiplying each element by 1/N. 7. Check for modular arithmetic correctness: N^{-1} mod BLS_MODULUS must be correctly computed.

checklist.title: Verify Supporting Node: Does divide_polynomialcoeff correctly perform long polynomial division for the quotient Q(X) = f(X)/Z(X)?

reachability.notes: The polynomial division must produce a correct quotient. The spec simplifies Q(X) = f(X)/Z(X) since deg(I(X)) < deg(Z(X)), meaning the remainder equals I(X) and the quotient is the same.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Verify that divide_polynomialcoeff implements standard long polynomial division correctly: iterating from highest degree to lowest. 2. Confirm that for f(X) of degree 4095 and Z(X) of degree 64, the quotient Q(X) has degree 4095 - 64 = 4031. 3. Mathematically verify: since f(X) = Q(X)*Z(X) + I(X) and deg(I(X)) < deg(Z(X)) = 64, the quotient Q(X) from divide_polynomialcoeff(f, Z) is correct regardless of remainder. 4. Test with a polynomial that IS exactly divisible by Z(X) and verify the quotient times Z(X) equals f(X). 5. Check for off-by-one errors in the loop: apos = len(a) - 1, bpos = len(b) - 1, diff = apos - bpos. 6. Verify field element division (quot = a[apos] / b[bpos]) uses correct modular inverse. 7. Test with polynomials where leading coefficients are zero to verify degree handling.

code_locations.notes: Long polynomial division. Iterates from highest to lowest degree, computing quotient coefficients.
Calls divide_polynomialcoeff(polynomial_coeff, denominator_poly) to compute quotient

checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0022 (SG-014-INV-001/003), Supporting node: actor-proof-generator. The spec comment says 'the computation can be simplified in monomial form to Q(X) = f(X) / Z(X)' because deg(I(X)) < deg(Z(X)). This means floor division of f by Z gives the same quotient as (f-I)/Z. The remainder of f/Z is I(X), but this does not affect the quotient.

Confirm that KZG_SETUP_G1_MONOMIAL points are valid BLS12-381 G1 points (on the curve and in the correct subgroup). 7. Test behavior when KZG_SETUP_G1_MONOMIAL is truncated or contains invalid points.

Test the complete pipeline: blob submission -> cell/proof generation -> gossip -> verification on receiving node. 8. Measure timing consistency: verify that proof generation time is bounded and does not vary significantly with blob content (timing side-channel resistance).

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does compute_kzg_proof_multi_impl enforce that the quotient polynomial degree does not exceed the trusted setup bound (len(KZG_SETUP_G1_MONOMIAL) - 1)?

reachability.notes: If recovery (SG-023) produces a higher-degree polynomial than expected, the quotient polynomial could exceed the trusted setup bounds.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify the exact length of KZG_SETUP_G1_MONOMIAL in each client implementation (should be at least FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_EXT_BLOB = 8192 points for Fulu). 2. Determine the maximum expected quotient polynomial degree: for a blob polynomial of degree FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB - 1 = 4095 and a vanishing polynomial of degree FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_CELL = 64, the expected quotient degree is 4095 - 64 = 4031. 3. Verify that implementations explicitly check len(quotient_polynomial) <= len(KZG_SETUP_G1_MONOMIAL) before calling g1_lincomb, and that exceeding this bound triggers a hard error (not silent truncation or out-of-bounds read). 4. Construct a pathological scenario: craft adversarial cells for recover_cells_and_kzg_proofs (SG-024) such that recover_polynomialcoeff (SG-023) reconstructs a polynomial with degree >= FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_EXT_BLOB (8192) by supplying exactly 50% of cells with corrupted data that passes the minimum-count assertion but produces an oversized polynomial. 5. Verify that recover_polynomialcoeff truncates to poly_coeff[:FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB] (INV-003 of SG-023), preventing higher-degree terms from propagating. 6. Test: if the truncation in step 5 fails or is bypassed, confirm that compute_kzg_proof_multi_impl still rejects the oversized quotient polynomial at the g1_lincomb call site. 7. In C/C++ implementations (c-kzg-4844), verify that the quotient coefficient array is bounds-checked against the SRS array length. A buffer overflow or out-of-bounds read on KZG_SETUP_G1_MONOMIAL would be a memory safety vulnerability. 8. In Go/Rust implementations, verify that an out-of-range index on the trusted setup slice triggers a panic or error, not silent behavior.

code_locations.notes: The critical call: proof = g1_lincomb(KZG_SETUP_G1_MONOMIAL, quotient_polynomial). If len(quotient_polynomial) > len(KZG_SETUP_G1_MONOMIAL), the g1_lincomb receives mismatched arrays. The spec passes the full KZG_SETUP_G1_MONOMIAL (not a slice), but implementations typically slice to len(quotient).

Returns PolynomialCoeff(poly_coeff[:FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB]). This truncation is a critical safety measure. If corrupted cells cause intermediate polynomials with degree >= FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_EXT_BLOB, the truncation bounds the output. But if the truncation is off-by-one or missing, the degree bound is violated.
Calls recover_polynomialcoeff then compute_cells_and_kzg_proofs_polynomialcoeff. This is the attack entry point: an attacker controls which cells are submitted for recovery.
Computes the quotient. If the numerator has unexpected high-degree terms, the quotient degree increases proportionally: deg(Q) = deg(f) - deg(Z).
Accepts points and scalars arrays. If scalars (quotient coefficients) is longer than points (SRS), behavior is implementation-defined: crash, silent truncation, or out-of-bounds read.

checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0023 (SG-014-INV-002), Trust Boundary: tb-004. The attack vector is: an attacker broadcasts corrupted cells via P2P that satisfy the 50% minimum for recovery, but the corrupted data causes recover_polynomialcoeff to reconstruct a polynomial with higher degree than expected. When this polynomial is fed into compute_cells_and_kzg_proofs_polynomialcoeff -> compute_kzg_proof_multi_impl, the quotient Q(X) = f(X)/Z(X) could have degree exceeding the trusted setup bound. The spec defends against this by truncating to poly_coeff[:FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB] in recover_polynomialcoeff, but implementations must faithfully implement this truncation. Defense-in-depth requires g1_lincomb to also reject oversized scalar arrays. A failure here means: (a) in C, potential buffer overflow reading past KZG_SETUP_G1_MONOMIAL, (b) in safe languages, a panic or invalid proof, (c) in all cases, a potential consensus split if different clients handle the error differently.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does recover_polynomialcoeff (SG-023) correctly bound the output polynomial degree to FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB - 1 before it enters the proof generation pipeline?

reachability.notes: The recovery function is the primary defense against attacker-supplied cells producing oversized polynomials. The truncation to poly_coeff[:FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB] is a critical boundary enforcement.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Verify that recover_polynomialcoeff returns PolynomialCoeff(poly_coeff[:FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB]) -- i.e., the output is truncated to at most FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB (4096) coefficients. 2. Construct adversarial recovery scenarios: provide exactly CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB / 2 (64) cells, with cell data chosen to maximize the degree of the recovered polynomial in the intermediate steps. 3. Trace the internal computation: (a) ez_eval = zero_poly_eval * extended_evaluation produces a polynomial of degree up to FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_EXT_BLOB - 1. (b) ez_coeffs from the inverse FFT may have non-zero coefficients beyond degree FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB - 1. (c) The coset FFT division reconstructs the full polynomial. (d) The final inverse coset FFT produces poly_coeff with up to FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_EXT_BLOB coefficients. 4. Verify that the truncation poly_coeff[:FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB] is an exact slice (not off-by-one: should be indices 0 through FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB - 1 = 4095). 5. Verify that for a legitimate blob, all coefficients beyond index FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB - 1 are zero (i.e., the truncation is lossless for valid data). 6. Verify that if truncation discards non-zero coefficients (indicating corrupted or adversarial input), the resulting polynomial still produces verifiable proofs -- OR that verification fails deterministically on all clients. 7. Check that recover_polynomialcoeff does NOT return an error for adversarial inputs that merely have high-degree artifacts after recovery. The spec truncates silently; implementations must match this behavior. 8. In client implementations, verify the truncation is applied correctly: (a) In c-kzg-4844, check that the poly_coeff buffer is allocated with exactly FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB elements, not FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_EXT_BLOB. (b) In go-kzg-4844, check that the slice operation is poly_coeff[:FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB]. (c) In rust-kzg, check for equivalent truncation.
checklist.bug_class: Bounds Enforcement / Data Integrity at Trust Boundary

checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0023 (SG-014-INV-002), Trust Boundary: tb-004. This check focuses on the PRIMARY defense: the truncation in recover_polynomialcoeff. The recovery algorithm operates over the extended domain (FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_EXT_BLOB = 8192) and naturally produces a polynomial with coefficients at all 8192 positions. The truncation to FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB (4096) is what ensures the recovered polynomial fits within the trusted setup degree bound. If this truncation is missing or incorrect: (1) the quotient polynomial in compute_kzg_proof_multi_impl could have degree up to 8192 - 64 = 8128, far exceeding the normal 4031, (2) g1_lincomb would attempt to use setup elements beyond the SRS length, (3) different clients would handle this differently, causing consensus divergence.

checklist.title: Verify Supporting Node: Does g1_lincomb provide defense-in-depth by rejecting or correctly handling cases where the scalar array length exceeds the trusted setup G1 point array length?

reachability.notes: g1_lincomb is the last line of defense before an oversized quotient polynomial produces an invalid commitment. Even if upstream truncation fails, g1_lincomb should not produce undefined behavior.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Review the g1_lincomb specification: it computes sum(scalars[i] * points[i]) for i in range(len(scalars)). Verify whether the spec requires len(scalars) == len(points) or allows mismatched lengths. 2. In c-kzg-4844: (a) Check if g1_lincomb_fast has an explicit assert(num_scalars <= num_points). (b) If not, check if blst_p1s_mult_pippenger has internal bounds checking. (c) Test: call g1_lincomb with num_scalars > num_points and verify the behavior (crash, error, or silent corruption). 3. In go-kzg-4844: (a) Check if the Go slice bounds are enforced. (b) Test with mismatched slice lengths. 4. In rust-kzg: (a) Check if the Rust implementation panics or returns Result::Err for mismatched lengths. 5. Verify that in the normal happy path, the quotient polynomial length (4032 coefficients) is always less than len(KZG_SETUP_G1_MONOMIAL). 6. Verify that even in the recovery path (recover_cells_and_kzg_proofs), the quotient polynomial length cannot exceed the trusted setup length due to the truncation in recover_polynomialcoeff. 7. Add a defense-in-depth assertion: at the call site in compute_kzg_proof_multi_impl, assert len(quotient) <= len(KZG_SETUP_G1_MONOMIAL) before calling g1_lincomb.

checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0023 (SG-014-INV-002), Supporting node: actor-kzg-trusted-setup. This is the defense-in-depth check. The primary defense is the truncation in recover_polynomialcoeff (CHK-0009). But if that truncation fails, g1_lincomb is the last safety net. In C implementations, an out-of-bounds read on the SRS array could expose memory or crash the node. In safe languages, a panic would cause node downtime (DoS). The expected behavior should be a clean error, not undefined behavior.

checklist.title: Verify End-to-End: Can an attacker trigger the recovery path (SG-023/SG-024) with adversarial cells to produce a polynomial whose quotient exceeds the trusted setup degree bound, causing proof generation failure or invalid proofs?

reachability.notes: End-to-end test of the full attack path described in the property. An attacker controls cell data via P2P gossip and can influence the recovery path.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Set up the attack scenario: (a) An attacker broadcasts exactly 64 cells (minimum 50% threshold for recovery) for a blob via P2P gossip. (b) The cells contain valid-format data (passes cell_to_coset_evals parsing) but the underlying evaluations do NOT correspond to a polynomial of degree < FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB. 2. Call recover_cells_and_kzg_proofs with these adversarial cells. 3. Trace the recovery computation through recover_polynomialcoeff: (a) The extended_evaluation is constructed with zeros for missing cells. (b) The vanishing polynomial for the 64 missing cell indices is constructed. (c) The FFT-based recovery algorithm produces poly_coeff. (d) Verify: does poly_coeff have non-zero coefficients at indices >= FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB? 4. After truncation to poly_coeff[:FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB], feed the recovered polynomial into compute_cells_and_kzg_proofs_polynomialcoeff. 5. Verify that all generated proofs either: (a) correctly verify against the blob commitment (if the recovery produced a valid polynomial), or (b) fail verification deterministically on all clients. 6. Crucially: verify there is NO scenario where proofs generated from adversarial recovery PASS verification on some clients but FAIL on others (consensus split). 7. Test with the original blob commitment: if the adversarial cells do not match the original blob, the recovered polynomial will differ, and proofs will fail verification against the original commitment. Verify this failure is consistent. 8. Test an edge case: what if the attacker provides exactly CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB / 2 legitimate cells and the remaining cells are naturally zero? This could produce a polynomial that is legitimate but exercises the maximum degree path.

code_locations.notes: Public entry point for recovery. Receives cell_indices and cells from P2P network. Validates bounds, then delegates to recover_polynomialcoeff and compute_cells_and_kzg_proofs_polynomialcoeff.
Core recovery algorithm. The truncation to poly_coeff[:FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB] is the critical degree bounding step.
Called after recovery to generate all cells and proofs from the recovered polynomial. Each call to compute_kzg_proof_multi_impl produces a quotient polynomial.
The function that produces the quotient polynomial. Degree of quotient = deg(recovered_poly) - FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_CELL. If recovery truncation works correctly, max quotient degree = 4095 - 64 = 4031.
Verification function used by receiving nodes. Must reject proofs generated from corrupted recovery.

executable_checks: End-to-end adversarial test: generate a valid blob, compute cells, corrupt 50% of cells, attempt recovery, verify recovered proofs fail against the original commitment
Edge case: supply exactly 64 cells with evaluation data that encodes a polynomial of degree FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_EXT_BLOB - 1, verify recover_polynomialcoeff truncates correctly
Cross-client consistency test: run the same adversarial recovery on all KZG libraries, verify identical error handling behavior
Invariant assertion: after every call to recover_polynomialcoeff, assert deg(result) < FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB
Stress test: fuzz recover_cells_and_kzg_proofs with random cell data and verify no memory errors, panics, or inconsistent proof validity across runs
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0023 (SG-014-INV-002), Trust Boundary: tb-004. This is the end-to-end attack path test. The attack vector: (1) attacker broadcasts corrupted cells via P2P, (2) honest node attempts data recovery, (3) recovery produces a polynomial that may have unexpected degree, (4) proof generation operates on this polynomial. The defense chain is: recover_polynomialcoeff truncation -> g1_lincomb bounds check. If both fail, the quotient polynomial exceeds the SRS, and the commitment is computed with insufficient setup elements, yielding an unpredictable G1 point. This could manifest as: (a) crash in unsafe languages, (b) panic in safe languages, (c) invalid proof that some clients accept and others reject. Bug bounty note: demonstrating a recovery path that produces a polynomial exceeding the setup degree bound would be a CRITICAL finding.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is the pairing equation e(LL, LR) == e(RL, [1]) correctly implemented with all terms (RLC, RLI, RLP) computed faithfully per the specification?

reachability.notes: Batch verification is the primary cryptographic gatekeeper. An attacker submits cells, commitments, and proofs for verification. Any error in the verification equation allows forged data to be accepted.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify the implementation of verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch_impl and locate the final pairing_check call. 2. Verify the pairing equation matches the specification: pairing_check([[LL, LR], [RL, neg(KZG_SETUP_G2_MONOMIAL[0])]]). 3. Confirm LL = g1_lincomb(proofs, r_powers) uses the correct linear combination of proofs weighted by random challenge powers. 4. Confirm LR = KZG_SETUP_G2_MONOMIAL[n] where n = FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_CELL (not FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB or other constant). 5. Verify RL = RLC - RLI + RLP with the correct sign convention (subtraction of RLI, addition of RLP). 6. Construct a known-valid set of commitments, cells, and proofs, then verify the pairing check returns True. 7. Construct a set with one tampered cell (e.g., flip one byte in coset_evals) and verify the pairing check returns False. 8. Construct a set with a tampered proof and verify rejection. 9. Test with edge case: single cell in the batch. 10. Test with edge case: maximum number of cells from multiple blobs.

checklist.title: Verify Fiat-Shamir Challenge Binding: Does compute_verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch_challenge include ALL verifier-relevant data (including all deduplicated commitments) in its hash input?

reachability.notes: A Weak Fiat-Shamir vulnerability was previously found in c-kzg-4844 where the challenge did not account for all deduplicated commitments. This is a known vulnerability class for this exact function.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Locate the implementation of compute_verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch_challenge. 2. Verify that the hash input includes ALL of the following in the correct order: (a) RANDOM_CHALLENGE_KZG_CELL_BATCH_DOMAIN domain separator, (b) FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB and FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_CELL constants, (c) len(commitments) and len(cell_indices), (d) ALL commitments (deduplicated list), (e) For each k: commitment_indices[k], cell_indices[k], all coset_eval values, proofs[k]. 3. Verify the hash input ordering is deterministic and canonical. 4. Verify that the FULL deduplicated commitments list is hashed (not just the commitments referenced by the batch). This was the root cause of the Weak Fiat-Shamir bug in c-kzg-4844 (#607). 5. Construct two different batches that differ only in an unused commitment and verify they produce different challenges. 6. Verify the domain separator RANDOM_CHALLENGE_KZG_CELL_BATCH_DOMAIN is correctly applied and prevents cross-protocol reuse of challenges.

checklist.title: Verify RLC Computation: Are commitment weights correctly accumulated from r_powers using commitment_indices, and does g1_lincomb correctly handle all edge cases including point-at-infinity?

reachability.notes: An attacker controls the commitments. If weight accumulation is incorrect, the wrong commitments are verified, potentially allowing forged proofs.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Verify the weight accumulation loop: for each k, weights[commitment_indices[k]] += r_powers[k]. 2. Test with multiple cells referencing the same commitment (weights must be summed, not overwritten). 3. Test with a single commitment referenced by all cells. 4. Test with each commitment referenced by exactly one cell. 5. Verify that g1_lincomb(commitments, weights) correctly handles the case where some weights are zero. 6. Verify g1_lincomb correctly handles point-at-infinity inputs in the commitments list. This is a KNOWN BUG CLASS: c-kzg-4844 previously had a bug where point-at-infinity filtering was removed from g1_lincomb_fast, causing incorrect results. 7. Test with a commitment that is the point at infinity and verify correct behavior. 8. Verify that the commitment_indices mapping from the deduplication step correctly preserves the association between cells and their original commitments.

code_locations.notes: Weight accumulation uses += which must be additive, not assignment
Deduplication must preserve semantic equivalence

checklist.title: Verify RLI Computation: Is the interpolation polynomial summation sum_k(r^k * interpolation_poly_k(s)) correctly computed using proper coset evaluation domains?

reachability.notes: The attacker provides cell evaluations (cosets_evals). If the interpolation polynomial is incorrectly computed, the verification equation could accept forged evaluations.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Verify that for each cell k, the interpolation polynomial is computed over coset_for_cell(cell_indices[k]) with the corresponding cosets_evals[k]. 2. Verify the interpolation polynomial has degree < FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_CELL (n). 3. Verify the scaling by r_powers[k] is correctly applied via polynomial multiplication (not scalar multiplication of the result). 4. Verify the accumulation into sum_interp_polys_coeff uses add_polynomialcoeff, not replace. 5. Verify the initial value sum_interp_polys_coeff is PolynomialCoeff([0] * n) with exactly n zero coefficients. 6. Verify RLI = g1_lincomb(KZG_SETUP_G1_MONOMIAL[:n], sum_interp_polys_coeff) uses the FIRST n elements of the SRS (not some other slice). 7. Test with cell evaluations that are all zeros and verify the interpolation polynomial is the zero polynomial. 8. Test with cell evaluations of a known polynomial and verify the interpolation matches.

code_locations.notes: Interpolation, scaling, and accumulation of polynomial evaluations
Lagrange interpolation correctness is critical for RLI
Coset domain must match the cell index

Unit test: verify sum_interp_polys_coeff has at most n coefficients after accumulation

checklist.title: Verify RLP Computation: Are the coset shift powers h_k^n correctly computed and applied to r_powers for the proof aggregation term?

reachability.notes: The RLP term binds each proof to its specific coset. An error in the coset shift computation would break the verification equation and could allow proof substitution.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Verify that for each cell k, h_k = coset_shift_for_cell(cell_indices[k]) returns the correct coset generator. 2. Verify h_k^n is computed as h_k.pow(FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_CELL), not h_k.pow(FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB) or other exponent. 3. Verify weighted_r_powers[k] = r_powers[k] * h_k^n (multiplication order should not matter for field elements, but verify). 4. Verify RLP = g1_lincomb(proofs, weighted_r_powers) uses the same proofs list as LL. 5. Verify coset_shift_for_cell uses bit_reversal_permutation correctly on roots of unity of the full extended domain. 6. Test: for a known coset, manually compute h_k^n and compare with the implementation. 7. Test: verify that different cell_indices produce different h_k values (no collisions). 8. Test: verify that cell_index = 0 produces the expected first coset shift.

code_locations.notes: Coset shift power computation and weighted random power accumulation
Must return the correct coset generator for each cell index

Unit test: verify h_k^n matches manually computed values for known cell indices
Unit test: verify weighted_r_powers computation matches spec for a known r and known cell_indices
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0024, SG-016 invariants (coset shift correctness). The exponent n = FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_CELL = 64 in mainnet config. A common error is using the wrong power or the wrong roots of unity order.

checklist.title: Verify RL Assembly and Final Pairing: Is RL = RLC - RLI + RLP correctly assembled with proper elliptic curve point arithmetic, and is the pairing check invoked with the correct arguments?

reachability.notes: The final assembly combines three G1 points. A sign error (e.g., RLC + RLI instead of RLC - RLI) would completely break the verification equation.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Verify RL computation: rl = bls.add(rlc, bls.neg(rli)) then rl = bls.add(rl, rlp). The subtraction of RLI must use bls.neg(), not just subtraction. 2. Verify the pairing check call: pairing_check([[ll, lr], [rl, neg(KZG_SETUP_G2_MONOMIAL[0])]]). 3. Confirm that KZG_SETUP_G2_MONOMIAL[0] is the G2 generator (tau^0 = [1]_2) and it is negated on the right side. 4. Verify the pairing check convention: the implementation checks e(LL, LR) * e(RL, -[1]_2) == 1, which is equivalent to e(LL, LR) == e(RL, [1]_2). 5. Test with a known-valid batch where the pairing check should return True. 6. Test with RL intentionally computed as RLC + RLI + RLP (wrong sign) and verify it fails. 7. Test with RL = RLC - RLI - RLP (wrong sign on RLP) and verify it fails. 8. Verify that the bls library's pairing_check function correctly implements the bilinear pairing equation.

checklist.title: Verify KZG Trusted Setup Usage: Are the correct elements from KZG_SETUP_G1_MONOMIAL and KZG_SETUP_G2_MONOMIAL used at the correct indices throughout the verification?

Verify that the SRS is loaded from the correct trusted setup file (the official Ethereum KZG ceremony output). 5. Verify that n = FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_CELL throughout (not FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB or FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_EXT_BLOB). 6. Test: manually verify that KZG_SETUP_G2_MONOMIAL[0] is indeed the G2 generator point. 7. Test: verify KZG_SETUP_G1_MONOMIAL[0] is the G1 generator point. 8. Verify no off-by-one errors in the SRS slice [:n] (should include indices 0 through n-1).
